The type SBD11B is a single phase, high speed, high impedance, static 
differential relay. It was specially designed to provide differential protection 
for high and low voltage AC busses. However, because of its design and 
sensitivity, this relay may also be used for shunt reactor differential 
protection. While the normal bus scheme requires three SBD11B relays one per 
phase the number of relays required for the protection shunt reactor depends on 
the scheme employed.

The first preliminary steps to prepare for relay testing describes the 
activities required prior to testing. Some of these steps could be performed 
days before the actual test. The second section Preparation for testing 
describes the steps to set up the equipment for performing the actual tests. The 
third section is the actual test.

Introduction
The type SBD11B is a single phase, high speed, high impedance, static 
differential relay. It was specially designed to provide differential protection 
for high and low voltage AC busses. However, because of its design and 
sensitivity, this relay may also be used for shunt reactor differential 
protection. While the normal bus scheme requires three SBD11B relays one per 
phase the number of relays required for the protection shunt reactor depends on 
the scheme employed.
The first preliminary steps to prepare for relay testing describes the 
activities required prior to testing. Some of these steps could be performed 
days before the actual test. The second section Preparation for testing 
describes the steps to set up the equipment for performing the actual tests. The 
third section is the actual test.
The first draft is initiated and tested by Eng. 
Saber Mohamed and Eng.Ragab Abd Elgwad, accepted by Eng. Mahmoud Badawy, 
Electrical Maintenance and Protection Manager, and approved by Eng. Ahmed Moussa 
Executive Operation and Maintenance Manager, revised by quality control head

Carefully follow these test procedure steps.
Verify the test results match the relay

Preparation
This procedure is used to perform off load 
 relay testing.
Look at the panel nameplate and check that 
 this system designation agrees with the generator that has been taken out of 
 service for maintenance.
Check there is no AC current from CTs by 
 using a clip on ammeter.
Testing Procedure 
(s)
Pick up Voltage 
Test
Connect the circuit as in Fig1.
Adjust the sverker to 95 volt AC (voltage tap 
 = 50).
Apply this voltage to the relay as shown in 
 fig. 1.
Increase the voltage until the voltmeter 
 begins to decrease and the ammeter to increase.
Record the value before the voltmeter begins 
 to decrease (100 4).
Pick 
up Current and Output Test
Connect the circuit as in Fig 2
Adjust the tape voltage setting to 50 and the 
 tape current setting to 0.5
Increase the current until the lamp 
 light.
Record the ammeter reading.
Tap Voltage Test
Connect the circuit as in Fig 3
Adjust the voltage tape setting to 50.
Apply 5 volt AC (10% of tape voltage) between 
 the terminals 5&6.
Read the volt between 5&16 (5V 2%)
Repeat the above four steps but with voltage 
 tape setting = 100.
Repeat the above four steps but with voltage 
 tape setting = 150.
Cautions
If the DC supply is 
 removed, studs 5&6 should be shorted by pulling the connection plug
Dont apply voltage to 
 the relay longer than 10 seconds and dont re-apply voltage more often than 
 once every 2 minutes
Return Relay and 
Associated Equipment to Service
Verify the test results match the 
 relay setting, if not consult technical services.
Trip the circuit breaker associated 
 with the relay.
Return relay to service by removing 
 the test leads from the relay terminals block and the test set. Make sure CT 
 secondary circuit is in normal condition.
Any equipment associated with the 
 relay which has been isolated, must be returned to service by the following 
 restoration steps:
Breaker trip coils.
Disturbance alarm and fault 
 recorder associated with this relay.
